proposed.explanation: Describes a straightforward project suited to percentage-of-PCC due to predictable scope and cost; not appropriate for MDPE. Simple mechanical systems and standard design suggest percentage-of-PCC viability, not MDPE. Standard office buildings with predictable costs favor percentage-of-PCC, not MDPE. Renovation projects with uncertain scope, phased delivery, or projects with difficult-to-estimate costs are well-suited to MDPE because hourly billing accommodates uncertainty better than percentage-of-PCC. MDPE protects the architect on projects where scope uncertainty and existing conditions make cost estimates unreliable.
